subject: Integration handshake & escalation playbook — CatalystCloud overlap
messages:
From: Leah Morgan <leah@catalystcloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@systems-int.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration handshake & account routing (CatalystCloud)

Hi Olga —

Great to meet briefly on Friday. We ran through initial SOW scope with our technical team and we have two overlapping enterprise pilots in Frankfurt and Munich that both map to existing Redwood reps. CatalystCloud prefers a single integration owner for onboarding (PM + technical lead) to avoid duplicated engineering tickets.

Can Redwood provide a short escalation/playbook for when account ownership is unclear? We want to avoid duplicate active projects and billing confusion. Attaching the pilot summaries.

Thanks,
Leah
Leah Morgan
Head of Partnerships, CatalystCloud
leah@catalystcloud.com
+44 7788 992233

Attachments: catalyst-integration-gap-analysis.pdf (pdf, 420KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Morgan <leah@catalystcloud.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@systems-int.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration handshake & account routing (CatalystCloud)

Leah —

Thanks for the context and the attach. We're happy to avoid duplication. I sketched a short playbook below that we've used for previous ISV integrators; happy to iterate. Key points:

- Single integration owner: we nominate the Redwood Integration Lead (technical) + Partner Success Manager as the commercial owner.
- Territory check: if both pilots are within the same legal entity and have one primary buying contact, the partner-owned integration model applies; otherwise assign to the nearest Redwood AE and flag as shared.
- Escalation window: 48H to resolve owner ambiguity; after that, integration work pauses until an owner is confirmed to protect engineering capacity.
- Billing handshake: billable work outside the pilot scope requires a signed change order and a single billing owner.

I'll propose concrete owners after Jonas confirms territory mapping. Attaching our pricing matrix so Catalyst can see effort buckets.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Alliances Operations
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: 101-pricing-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 85KB); escalation-routing-playbook.docx (docx, 60KB)

Olga / team —

I pulled the CRM records for the two pilots in question (CatalystCloud: Frankfurt pilot ID F-912 and Munich pilot ID M-331). Preliminary notes:

- F-912 is owned by AE: Marissa Cole (assigned 2028-05-02).
- M-331 currently sits in unassigned queue but was sourced by a channel referral (CatalystCloud) and was routed to EMEA inbound.

Recommendation: designate Marissa as primary integration owner for both pilots under a shared account model, with CatalystCloud as partner integrator co-owner for technical tasks. This avoids duplicate contacts and keeps billing simple (Marissa's AE team will own commercial changes).

If Marissa approves, I'll open a single integration ticket and mark both pilots with shared-owner tags.

-Jonas
